To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The Arabidopsis thialiana nit2/nit/nit3 gene family encodes nitrilases which catalyze the terminal activation step of indole-3-acetamide (IAA) and phenylacetaldoxime (PAO) to indole-3- acetic acid (IAA) or phenylacetic acid (PAA), respectively; (2) The three genes are arranged as a cluster in the Arabidopsis genome

the nit2, nit3 and nit1 genes encode nitrilases which catalyze the terminal step in indole-3-acetic acid biosynthetic pathway, and that the genes show a high degree of structural conservation, but differ in their expression pattern.
the nit1 promoter is active in leaves, shoot apex and root tip of transgenic tobacco, and that the nit1 gene is active in the root tip of wild-type Arabidopsis thalania.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular basis of auxin homeostasis and its regulation.
the elucidation of the genetic basis of auxin biosynthetic processes.
the elucidation of the biosynthesis of the plant hormone indole-acetic (indole-3) acid (IAA) from the precursor indole.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nitrilases are not involved in the biosynthesis of auxin in Arabidopsis.
nitrilase expression patterns do not support a role for the nit1 gene in indole-acetamide biosynthesis in Arabdiopsis thaliana.
nitrilases are involved in the biosynthesis of indole-3-acetic acid, and that the nit3 isoform may be the major contributor to this process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nitrilases are involved in the synthesis of indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) from tryptophan and that their expression is regulated by developmental programs and environmental factors.

the nitrilases are the terminal activation enzymes in auxin biosynthesis, that they are encoded by three highly conserved genes in Arabidopsis, and that their expression is tightly controlled by a complex regulatory system.
the nit2/nir1/nit3 nitrilase genes are expressed in all tissues of the plant, but that the level of expression varies considerably.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nitrilases are not only involved in the biosynthesis of the plant hormone auxin, but that they also are involved in the regulation of the auxin level in the plant.
nitrilase expression is not restricted to the shoot apex and the root tip, but is also observed in other tissues of the plant.
nitrilases are involved in the biosynthesis of indole-acetic-acid in Arabidopsis.
